parameters.name: -Scope
parameters.description: Specifies the scope affected by the execution policy.

parameters.name: -Confirm
parameters.description: Prompts for confirmation before running the cmdlet.

parameters.name: -WhatIf
parameters.description: Shows what would happen if the cmdlet runs, without executing it.

details.description: Requires all scripts and configuration files, including locally written ones, to be signed by a trusted publisher.
Nothing is blocked; no warnings or prompts are displayed.
Sets the default execution policy. This is `Restricted` for Windows clients and `RemoteSigned` for Windows servers.
Requires all scripts and configuration files downloaded from the Internet to be signed by a trusted publisher. Default for Windows server computers.
Does not load configuration files or run scripts. Default for Windows client computers.
No execution policy is set for the scope. Removes an assigned execution policy from a scope not set by Group Policy. If all scopes are `Undefined`, the effective policy is `Restricted`.

Loads all configuration files and runs all scripts. For unsigned scripts downloaded from the internet, prompts for permission before running. Default for non-Windows computers (PowerShell 6.0+), cannot be changed on these platforms.
Set by a Group Policy for all users of the computer. Cannot be directly changed by `Set-ExecutionPolicy`.
Set by a Group Policy for the current user of the computer. Cannot be directly changed by `Set-ExecutionPolicy`.
Affects only the current PowerShell session. Policy saved in `$Env:PSExecutionPolicyPreference` and deleted when the session closes.
Default scope, affects all users of the computer (stored in `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE`). Requires 'Run as Administrator' to change.
Affects only the current user (stored in `HKEY_LOCAL_USER`).

features.name: Checking Execution Policy
details: `Get-ExecutionPolicy -List`: Displays execution policies for each scope.
`Get-ExecutionPolicy`: Shows the effective execution policy for the current PowerShell session.

features.name: Bypassing Policy for Specific Files
details: `Unblock-File -Path <script_path>`: Unblocks a specific script downloaded from the internet, allowing it to run without changing the current execution policy. User should review script code first.
